claims.text: Ask: what they're proud of; the child's abilities, likes and dislikes; how the child does at home, preschool or child care; concerns about health or getting along with others; how the family and child are doing; family changes over the past year.
claims.quote: What are you most proud of about your child? (If the parent responds, “Nothing,” the clinician should be prepared with a compliment, such as, “You made time for this visit despite your busy schedule.”) • Tell me about his abilities and what he most likes and dislikes these days. • How is your child doing at home, preschool, or child care? • What questions or concerns do you have about him? His health? His ability to get along with other people? • How are things going for your family? • How are things going for your child? • What changes have occurred in your family over the past year?

claims.text: Past medical hx: any specialty or emergency care since the last visit.
claims.quote: received any specialty or emergency care since the last visit?
claims.locator: 4 year visit, Health Supervision: History / Review of Systems

claims.text: Family hx: any new health condition or death in the family; if yes, who has or had it, age at onset and diagnosis, or age at death.
claims.quote: developed a new health condition or died? If the answer is Yes: Ascertain who in the family has or had the condition, and ask about the age of onset and diagnosis. If the person is no longer living, ask about the age at the time of death.

claims.text: ROS — any problems with: headaches; vision or crossed eyes; ears, nose and throat; breathing or chest pain; nausea or vomiting, bowel movements; birthmarks or moles; muscle strength, movement or function; language.
